description: Turn an API (OpenAPI or Swagger spec), a Postgres or MySQL database, documents or a remote MCP server into a hosted MCP server for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex and other AI clients. Public API specs work with no account: one command gives a live MCP server and a claim link.
rules: To create a live MCP server from a public OpenAPI or Swagger spec with no account, run: npx @kaiva/bridge try --openapi <spec-url> (add --json for machine-readable output).

Without the CLI, send POST https://api.kaiv.ai/api/bridge/claimable with JSON {"specUrl": "<spec-url>"} or {"spec": "<spec text>"}. The answer has mcpUrl, apiKey (shown once, sent as Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>), claimUrl, expiresAt and tools.
A server created without an account offers only the spec's GET operations, accepts no credentials, and lasts 72 hours or 500 tool calls. Never send credentials to it; they are refused.

Always give the user the claimUrl. Claiming keeps the server in their Kaiva Bridge workspace at the same address, under their plan; the apiKey stops working then, and they connect their AI client again from the server's Connect tab.

For private APIs, databases, documents or tools that change data, sign in first: npx @kaiva/bridge login, then npx @kaiva/bridge push <name> --openapi <spec-url> (or --postgres, --mysql, --docs, --mcp).
In a cloud agent sandbox such as Codex cloud or Claude Code on the web, allow the domains api.kaiv.ai and registry.npmjs.org before running these commands.
